title: Power and Ground
summary: Electricity is like a train on a circular railway track: it must travel in a complete, unbroken loop!

steps.title: Power and Ground
steps.markdownContent: A circuit needs a complete path. For this LED activity, use the kit’s resistor in series with the LED. Unplug the board before changing wires.

quickCheck.question: What does electricity need in order to flow and light up a bulb?
options: A complete, unbroken loop from power to ground
A broken wire with a big gap in it
quickCheck.explanation: Electricity can only flow when there is a complete, unbroken circle (circuit) from power back to ground!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: The word 'circuit' means circle! Electricity must travel in a full circle from power back to ground.

quickCheck.question: What does the label 'GND' stand for on the Arduino board?
options: Ground — the return path for electric current
quickCheck.explanation: GND stands for Ground! It is the essential return path for electricity in every circuit.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: GND is short for Ground. In electronics, Ground is the safe return route for electric current.

steps.title: The Closed Electrical Highway
steps.markdownContent: Follow the path: 5V → resistor → LED → GND. If the path breaks, the LED turns off. A wire straight from 5V to GND makes an unsafe short.

steps.title: Ground Troubleshooting Lab
steps.markdownContent: Build or inspect the LED path. Try the complete circuit, a missing connection, and the short-circuit diagram. Never build a direct 5V-to-GND short.

steps.title: Power & Ground Checkpoint
steps.markdownContent: Verify your understanding of electrical circuits, power, and ground!

interactiveConfig.question: What happens if the Ground (GND) wire falls out of a working LED circuit?
options: The circuit opens, electrons stop flowing, and the LED turns OFF
The LED turns into a laser beam
The LED turns bright purple forever
interactiveConfig.explanation: Without Ground, there is no return path for current, creating an open circuit where electricity cannot flow.
